messages:
maria (support): FYI customer ryan reported a huge spike in retries and token usage overnight. they get lots of 429s then the python SDK kicks off many concurrent retries -> cost spike. attaching initial notes.
ryan (customer): seeing 429 bursts after a partial outage, then the client retries hammer our Dedicated pool and we hit capacity. curious if idempotency keys might be getting dropped.
ryan (customer): stack traces attached in their support ticket, but logs show many identical request payloads replayed within <200ms windows.
maria (support): @olivia can you ask devx for immediate triage? customer on a paid Dedicated plan so we should prioritize.
olivia (devx): pinging eng. can you confirm sdk version + python runtime? also whether they're using asyncio client or sync?
ryan (customer): python 3.11, redwood-python 0.16.2, using AsyncClient with connection pool size default.
kai (eng): thanks. known-ish surface: earlier backoff scheduler bug where jitter reseed wasn't per-request under heavy concurrency. that could lead to synchronized retry times (thundering). need repro.
kai (eng): also curious about idempotency header preservation across retry attempts. if idempotency-key is dropped on retry we can double-charge. can you paste the request snippet?
maria (support): forwarded minimal snippet from customer: 
```
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x...")
async def call():
    for _ in range(100):
        await client.responses.create(model="redwood-1", input="ping")
```
ryan (customer): that's their simplified loop; real app uses many concurrent coroutines and an exponential backoff helper (custom).
kai (eng): notable: 0.16.2 included a change to the retry scheduler to reuse a global PRNG for jitter to avoid reseeding overhead. under high concurrency that caused correlated jitter in practice. also there's a separate bug where idempotency headers set on the outer request object are not copied into a reconstructed request on some retry codepaths.
kai (eng): repro suggestion: run an async test with 200 coroutines hitting a rate-limited endpoint, instrument timestamps of retries. i'll try to reproduce locally.
infra-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-us-west1 latency spike at 2026-11-09T02:14:23Z, 429 rate increased to 18% over baseline.
olivia (devx): customer says they saw duplicate side-effects twice. we need to confirm idempotency bug before rolling any fixes.
kai (eng): i spun up a quick repro script and observed clustered retry attempts ~ identical ms windows. here's trimmed log: 
```
[11:04:01.123] request id=aa-1 attempt=1 -> 429
[11:04:01.624] retry scheduled in 0.5s (jitter deterministic)
[11:04:01.125] request id=aa-2 attempt=1 -> 429
[11:04:01.626] retry scheduled in 0.5s (jitter deterministic)
[11:04:01.623] many requests all scheduled at ~0.5s
[11:04:01.623] retry attempt time collisions -> request storm
```
ryan (customer): logs also show that the second attempt sometimes has no Idempotency-Key header in the outgoing request trace (we log headers redacted except key presence).
kai (eng): confirmed one repro path: when using our AsyncClient with connection pooling + urllib3 connection reuse, on Retry.prepare_retry we reconstruct Request objects and we were not always copying over the user-supplied headers map (bug triggered when header mapping was a CaseInsensitiveDict vs dict).
mar ia (support): small typo in name in previous line: that's kai's note.
maria (support): next steps proposed: 1) immediate mitigation guidance to customer, 2) reproduce and write failing unit test, 3) patch and release hotfix (0.16.3+), 4) notify affected Dedicated customers.
olivia (devx): mitigation: set client retry policy to conservative and reduce max_concurrency; example config we can recommend: 
```
client = AsyncClient(..., max_concurrency=16, retry_policy={"max_attempts":3, "backoff_base":0.2, "jitter":"full"})
```
kai (eng): note: the SDK currently accepts jitter param but when global PRNG reuse is active jitter becomes deterministic across tasks. short-term mitigation: pin to 0.15.x or set environment var REDWOOD_JS_PRNG_RESEED=1 (we'll add a python-specific flag) — but we should not ask customers to env hack.
kai (eng): on the idempotency header drop i'll open a branch to ensure header dict is shallow-copied and normalized before retry. will add tests for CaseInsensitiveDict variants.
ryan (customer): appreciate the quick triage. do you have ETA for a fix? duplicates caused an extra charge we need to reconcile.
maria (support): noting billing team involvement. i'll open a ticket for refund/adjustment pending engineering confirmation.
kai (eng): i have a working patch, local tests pass. still running stress matrix. will open PR referencing this thread by EOD.
kai (eng): repro commands i used: 
```
# run within venv
python -m pytest tests/repro/test_thundering_retry.py -k stress -q
# stress config
CONCURRENCY=200 ITER=1000 python tests/repro/stress_runner.py
```
olivia (devx): i'll prepare a customer-safe advisory and rollout notes. if PR lands today we can cut 0.16.3 tomorrow and push a pinned changelog.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started for branch fix/retry-header-copy. CI: 38/42 passed, 4 flaky infra tests failing.
kai (eng): addressing flaky infra tests now. mainline patch includes: per-request PRNG seeding option, deep-copy header preservation on retry, and an integration test for duplicate side-effect prevention.
maria (support): thanks everyone. i'll update ryan with mitigation steps and timeline.
ryan (customer): thanks. please cc billing once fix is merged so we can reconcile costs.
olivia (devx): noted. will coordinate. :thumbsup:
